results.content: power map: degree d>=2 rational map conjugate to z -> z^{±d}
results.note: Definitional object used by Main Theorem and by the external Proposition 4; no proof owed.

results.content: Chebyshev map: conjugate to ±T_d; T_d fixed by T_d(z+z^{-1})=z^d+z^{-d} (prose construction lines 88-92)
Lattès map via commuting torus diagram; flexible Lattès map when p has degree 2 and L(z)=az+b with a in Z
results.figure_dependency: xymatrix commutative diagram lines 102-107; typeset diagram (xy package), no external image file

results.content: power/Chebyshev maps have only integer multipliers; a Lattès map has an imaginary quadratic K with all multipliers in O_K, and all multipliers are integers iff the map is flexible
results.note: Stated with citation only; no proof in this work. Motivates the converse; not an author result.

results.content: If K is a number field and f: P^1->P^1 has degree d>=2 with all multipliers in K, then f is a power map, a Chebyshev map or a Lattès map

proof_block.kind: proof environment titled 'Proof of Main Theorem'

results.note: Exactly the statement already carried by 2158 (old statement span 130-132, old proof span 269-305). Reused verbatim as to range; difficulty H3 reused unchanged per task scope.

results.content: Ji-Xie: for imaginary quadratic K, degree d>=2 rational map with all multipliers in O_K is power, Chebyshev or Lattès
results.note: Prior theorem cited for comparison; the paper notes the discreteness of O_K is essential there and that this work needs a different method (lines 143).

results.content: Autissier equidistribution: for f over a number field K and a sequence of nonempty pairwise disjoint Gal(Qbar/K)-invariant finite periodic-point sets S_n, the normalized counting measures converge weakly to mu_f
results.attribution: quoted, \cite[Prop. 4.1.4]{A2001}; analogies cited to BR2010 Th. 10.24 and FRL2006 Th. 2 & 4

results.content: Zdunik: a degree d>=2 rational map that is not a power, Chebyshev or Lattès map has infinitely many periodic points with characteristic exponent > Lyapunov exponent L_f
results.attribution: quoted, \cite[Prop. 4]{Z2014}, with the strengthening (one point -> infinitely many) discussed in Remark 8
results.note: The cited one-point characterization is used in the author infinite-point form with the concrete adaptation in Remark8; retain both as support, no separate new primary.

results.content: Author's account of how Zdunik's proof is modified (adjoin periodic points of period <= N to the critical values p_1..p_s when building the family B of balls, page 260 of Z2014) to obtain infinitely many rather than one such periodic point
results.note: Author explicitly specifies the Z2014 proof modification and derives arbitrarily large periods; preserve complete adaptation prose and cited input, not wholly omitted author mathematics.

results.content: If z_0 is a repelling periodic point of degree d>=2 map f with z_0 not in the postcritical set P_f, there is a sequence of periodic points w_n with pairwise distinct periods and chi_f(w_n) -> chi_f(z_0)
results.note: The complete author proof (shadowing the repeller via inverse branches g and h, forcing exact period n, then squeezing the multiplier) is precisely the construction already credited in 2158's H3 reason. Per scope it must not be split into a new problem nor re-audited.

results.content: Two comparisons: (i) Ji-Xie's Koenigs-linearization version gives periods n with multipliers rho_n = a lambda^n + b + o(1); (ii) 'one can show' that the closure of the set of characteristic exponents at cycles is a union of an interval and a finite set, a weak version of JX2022 Cor. 1.16
results.note: Contains the unproved phrase 'one can show' with a pointer to the proof of FG2022 Lem. 2.1 ('compare'); no proof is given here and the interval-non-singleton property is attributed to JX2022 Cor. 1.16. Recorded as open/unexpanded, not as an author-complete theorem.
